question: A sheet of paper is divided into 8 equal parts, and 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the sheet is shaded? Use \(1\div8\) to represent each part. Calculate: \(1\div8=?\) (Answer as a decimal.)
solution: Each part is \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the sheet. To find its decimal value, think of one whole as \(1000\) thousandths. Since \(125\times8=1000\), sharing these thousandths equally among \(8\) parts gives \(125\) thousandths per part. The first three places after the decimal point represent tenths, hundredths, and thousandths. Thus \(125\) thousandths is \(1\) tenth, \(2\) hundredths, and \(5\) thousandths, written \(0.125\). Since \(1\div8=\frac{1}{8}=0.125\), the requested decimal answer is \(0.125\).

edges.reason: The target explicitly includes the multiplication-division relation, so multiplication meaning is needed for that inverse-operation assertion.

Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.

Division introduces equal sharing, a useful conceptual bridge. Folding one whole into equal paper parts establishes a unit fraction without division notation or the inverse-multiplication interpretation.

The earlier concrete money/length treatment gives useful tenths experience. The later node itself introduces tenths and hundredths as decimal fractions, so the link is spiral preparation rather than a distinct necessary concept; Gemini equates reintroducing that content with mandatory prior instruction.
edges.scope: extending decimal meaning from tenths to hundredths

edges.reason: Two-digit integer division prepares legitimate two-digit-divisor cases. The stated criterion also permits a one-digit divisor, and the decimal-place extension can be learned from that simpler algorithm, so the entire two-digit trial-quotient method is not universal.

The target explicitly computes a one-place decimal divided by an integer and writes a decimal result; decimal-by-decimal multiplication is an unrelated procedure. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
edges.scope: Decimal place and value meanings when dividing a decimal dividend and writing a decimal quotient
